name: Saint Wenceslaus
history: Duke of Bohemia, raised in the faith by his grandmother Saint Ludmila. He ruled justly, built churches and cared for the poor, but his Christian rule and his peace with the Germans made him enemies. He was murdered by his brother Boleslav on his way to Mass. He is the patron saint of the Czech people.
life: Wenceslaus was the son of Duke Vratislav. After his father’s death his grandmother Ludmila brought him up a Christian, and in 921 she was murdered by nobles loyal to his mother, Drahomíra, who resented her influence. When he came of age Wenceslaus took up the government himself. He favoured the Church, welcomed priests from Bavaria, founded the rotunda of Saint Vitus in Prague and, to spare his land war, accepted the overlordship of the German king Henry the Fowler. Early lives tell of his charity, of his gathering wood for the poor by night and of his care for the bread and wine of the Mass. In 935, or perhaps 929, he went to Stará Boleslav at his brother’s invitation for the feast of Saints Cosmas and Damian. Next morning, on his way to Mass, he was struck down at the church door. The carol Good King Wenceslas is a Victorian invention, but true to his reputation.
prayerTo: Saint Wenceslaus, you ruled as a servant of Christ and met death on your way to Mass. Pray for all who hold power, that they may seek peace and justice, for families divided by envy and ambition, and for me, that I may love the Mass and be generous to the poor in their need. Amen.
penance: Give warm clothing, food or help with heating costs to someone in need today, and pray for reconciliation in a divided family.
meditation: Wenceslaus was killed by his own brother at the door of a church. Is there a brother or sister you need to forgive or be reconciled with?
prayer: O God, Who through the palm of martyrdom transported blessed Wenceslaus from an earthly dominion unto heavenly glory, keep us, by his prayers, from all harm and grant us to rejoice in his fellowship. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
